paper.title: SkillMOO: Multi-Objective Optimization of Agent Skills for Software Engineering
paper.central_claim: SE agent skill bundles should be treated as multi-objective search objects; SkillMOO evolves bundles via LLM-proposed edits (pruning, substitution, reordering, rewriting) and NSGA-II Pareto selection on pass rate and inference cost, achieving the top pass-rate rank on 11 of 12 non-zero-pass SkillsBench SE tasks with cost reductions up to 32.1% over static bundles and pass-rate gains up to 42 percentage points, and pruning/substitution dominate successful edits.
paper.claim_scope: 16 SkillsBench SE tasks (4 with zero pass for all methods), GLM-5 as solver and optimizer, population 4 x 3 generations, 10 runs per method per task, LLM-expanded 40-43-test verifiers.

signatures.object: Per-task skill bundle (subset and edited versions of the task SkillsBench skill pool: instructions, scripts, resources).
signatures.information: Per-candidate evaluation evidence: pass rate, cost, runtime, failure traces from the full verifier test suite (40-43 tests).
signatures.operation: Population 4, 3 generations. Optimizer agent (GLM-5) proposes remove/replace/add/reorder/rewrite edits per surviving bundle; solver agent (GLM-5) evaluates each child; NSGA-II ranks by (-pass, cost) with crowding distance and survivors breed the next generation.
signatures.output: Pareto archive of evaluated bundles; one bundle selected per run (selection rule from the archive not specified).
signatures.conditions: Per-candidate timeout 900 s; per-task budget about $1-$15 and under three hours.
signatures.feedback: Verifier pass/fail (oracle test suite for the same task) and measured USD cost/runtime.
signatures.selection_rule: NSGA-II non-dominated sorting on pass rate and cost.
signatures.selection_data: The same task and same verifier test suite used later to report results; candidates evaluated by the same solver.
signatures.persistence: Task-specific optimized bundle / Pareto archive that can be reused on the same task; routing/reuse across tasks is future work.
signatures.later_use: Reuse on repeated runs of the same task (break-even 5-682 reuses).
signatures.claimed_effect: Top pass-rate rank 11/12; Task 5 pass 0.16->0.37, cost -32.1%; average pass 0.39 vs 0.14 (ori_skill) and 0.21 (no_skill).
signatures.failure_boundary: Four tasks zero pass for all methods; no cross-task or cross-model transfer; edit analysis exploratory only; Add-skill edits never improved pass rate in the archive.

gap.author_gap: Agent skills are deployed as static hand-crafted assets or evolved on pass rate alone, although a skill can raise token cost or add misleading guidance, so pass rate and cost trade off.
gap.checked_gap: The trade-off is supported by cited external evidence (SkillsBench, SWE-Skills-Bench) and by the paper own Table 2, where the original bundles average lower pass (0.14) than no skills (0.21) and cost more than no skills. Pass-rate-only neighbors (EvoSkill, Meta Context Engineering, EvoSkills, ACE, GEPA, Meta-Harness) are named but not run; LLM-guided genetic improvement is the closest search precedent. The checked residue is narrow: cost-aware Pareto selection and pruning-dominant edits.
gap.lineage: Static curated skills (SkillsBench/SWE-Skills-Bench) -> pass-rate skill evolution (EvoSkill, EvoSkills) and context/prompt/harness optimizers (ACE, GEPA, Meta-Harness) -> LLM-guided GI with NSGA-II -> SkillMOO (cost-aware Pareto selection of skill bundles).
closest_adjacent: EvoSkill / EvoSkills / Meta Context Engineering: pass-rate-only skill evolution (E04)
LLM-guided Genetic Improvement: LLM edits + search-based software evolution (cited)
gap.residue: Skill bundles that raise cost or distract the agent; pass-only evolution ignores this.
gap.stakes: Up to 32.1% lower cost and 23.6% lower runtime with higher pass on the best task; typical search overhead $1.76-$13.73 per task.
gap.method_response: Treat bundle as a candidate in a bi-objective search; LLM edits informed by evaluation evidence; NSGA-II survivor selection.
gap.remaining_gap: No pass-only or budget-matched alternative search; cross-task/model transfer open; per-task optimization on the same verifier; mechanism of gains only descriptive.
unresolved: Whether cost-aware selection or LLM edits are needed relative to simple subset search at equal evaluation budget.
Whether reported SkillMOO pass rates are fresh re-evaluations or search-time outcomes.

claims.text: SkillMOO achieves the top pass-rate rank on 11 of 12 non-zero-pass tasks with lower cost than static bundles.
claims.setting: 16 SkillsBench SE tasks, GLM-5, 10 runs per method.
claims.baseline_control: ori_skill and no_skill; no equal-budget search baseline.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same task and same verifier used for fitness and reporting; fresh re-evaluation not stated.
claims.result_denominator: Mean +/- SD over 10 binary runs per task; Scott-Knott ESD ranks; 4 zero-pass tasks excluded from comparison but reported.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Per task, the search-selected bundle outperformed the original and empty bundles on the same verifier; the contribution of cost-aware selection or LLM edits versus any search is not isolated.

claims.text: Pruning and substitution are the dominant successful edit operations.
claims.selection_vs_test: Edits filtered from search traces with non-zero deltas.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive only (authors disclaim causality); Task 1 gains occurred with a single-skill bundle where pruning is impossible.
Plausible when the same task is repeated tens of times; one-shot tasks need a reliability argument.

claims.text: Treating skills as multi-objective objects is warranted over static or pass-only practice.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Motivated by static-bundle weakness (avg pass 0.14 vs 0.21 for no skill), but the benefit of the multi-objective part is not tested.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: For individual SkillsBench SE tasks, a small LLM-mutation + NSGA-II search over skill bundles found bundles with higher pass rate and often lower cost than the original or empty bundle on the same verifier suite (10 runs per task, GLM-5), at roughly $2-14 search cost per task.
not_supported: That multi-objective selection is needed (no pass-only/equal-budget arm).
Transfer of optimized bundles across tasks or models.
Causal role of pruning/substitution (authors say exploratory).
unresolved: Opus: the per-run pass-rate unit in Table 2 conflicts with the binary definition in §4 (opus:O01).
assessment.reproduction_note: Author-reported; not reproduced. Capped at task because selection and reporting share task and verifier.
